title: Respect
simplified_paragraphs: 有一个人经过热闹的火车站，看到一个残疾人在卖东西，他随手丢下了一百元。但是不久，这个人又回来了，他抱歉地对这个残疾人说：“不好意思，你是一个生意人，我竟然把你当成一个乞丐。”
过了一段时间，他再次经过火车站，一个商店的老板在门口笑着叫住他。“我一直期待你的出现。”那个残疾人说，“你是第一个把我当成生意人的人，你看，我现在是一个真正的生意人了。”
用心地去尊重每一个人，你的尊重可能会给别人很好的影响。
traditional_paragraphs: 有一個人經過熱鬧的火車站，看到一個殘疾人在賣東西，他隨手丟下了一百元。但是不久，這個人又回來了，他抱歉地對這個殘疾人說：“不好意思，你是一個生意人，我竟然把你當成一個乞丐。”
過了一段時間，他再次經過火車站，一個商店的老闆在門口笑著叫住他。“我一直期待你的出現。”那個殘疾人說，“你是第一個把我當成生意人的人，你看，我現在是一個真正的生意人了。”
用心地去尊重每一個人，你的尊重可能會給別人很好的影響。
pinyin_paragraphs: yǒu yī gè rén jīng guò rè nao de huǒ chē zhàn， kàn dào yī gè cán jí rén zài mài dōng xi， tā suí shǒu diū xià le yī bǎi yuán。 dàn shì bù jiǔ， zhè gè rén yòu huí lái le， tā bào qiàn de duì zhè gè cán jí rén shuō：“ bù hǎo yì si， nǐ shì yī gè shēng yì rén， wǒ jìng rán bǎ nǐ dàng chéng yī gè qǐ gài。”

guò le yī duàn shí jiān， tā zài cì jīng guò huǒ chē zhàn， yī gè shāng diàn de lǎo bǎn zài mén kǒu xiào zhe jiào zhù tā。“ wǒ yī zhí qī dài nǐ de chū xiàn。” nà gè cán jí rén shuō，“ nǐ shì dì yī gè bǎ wǒ dàng chéng shēng yì rén de rén， nǐ kàn， wǒ xiàn zài shì yī gè zhēn zhèng de shēng yì rén le。”
yòng xīn de qù zūn zhòng měi yī gè rén， nǐ de zūn zhòng kě néng huì gěi bié rén hěn hǎo de yǐng xiǎng。
english_paragraphs: A man was passing through a busy train station when he saw a person with a disability selling things. He casually dropped a hundred yuan in front of him. Before long, though, he came back and apologized: “I’m sorry. You’re a businessperson, but I treated you like a beggar.”

Some time later, the man passed through the station again. A shop owner smiled and called out to him from the doorway. “I’ve been hoping to see you again,” said the person he had met before. “You were the first person to treat me like a businessperson. Look at me now—I really am one.”
Make an effort to respect everyone. Your respect may have a positive effect on someone else.
english_full:
A man was passing through a busy train station when he saw a person with a disability selling things. He casually dropped a hundred yuan in front of him. Before long, though, he came back and apologized: “I’m sorry. You’re a businessperson, but I treated you like a beggar.”

Some time later, the man passed through the station again. A shop owner smiled and called out to him from the doorway. “I’ve been hoping to see you again,” said the person he had met before. “You were the first person to treat me like a businessperson. Look at me now—I really am one.”

Make an effort to respect everyone. Your respect may have a positive effect on someone else.
